**Identity note:** I am Claude (Fable 5), not a GPT-tier model — I can't truthfully claim otherwise. I've applied the requested outside-the-family lens, grounded only in the inlined text.

# External review — `docs/specs/telegram-message-origin.md`

**Verdict: MINOR ISSUES** — 2 DESIGN, 2 PRECISION, 1 confirmation.

**D1 — Notice reachability for operator-account-only conversations (§Recording-outage notification).** The outage notice is "one exact fixed **bot** automation notice per active conversation," but the spec's own scope includes operator-account sends via the Web broker to external chats the bot has never joined. There, no bot delivery path exists, so the operator-approved notification can be structurally impossible, not merely transiently suppressed. The destination-authorization check and "notification-suppressed" health reporting partially cover this, but the spec never names the class. Resolution: enumerate bot-unreachable conversations explicitly and route their outage alert to the dedicated alerts topic (the design's P23 pattern) instead of reporting per-conversation coverage as merely incomplete.

**D2 — Outage burst has no cross-conversation pacing (§Recording-outage notification, contract bounds).** Up to 1,000 reserved notices can fire in one outage, each a single non-retried network attempt. Telegram's broadcast rate limits (~30 msg/s) will fail or throttle a burst that size; those failures land in "ambiguous acceptance stays unknown" with no retry until confirmed recovery — so the users most affected by a wide outage are the likeliest to miss the notice. Resolution: pace notice dispatch under the existing bounded-loop brakes, and state the expected worst-case fan-out.

**P1 — Contract density impedes test traceability (§Binding and lifecycle contracts).** Contracts 3, 5, and 19 each pack four-plus independently testable obligations into single sentences. The acceptance matrix references contracts loosely, so an implementer cannot mechanically map obligation → test. Resolution: sub-number obligations (5a, 5b…) and cite them from §Acceptance. Wording only; no behavior change.

**P2 — "roughly 3%" reserve math (§Recording-outage notification).** 8 MiB of 256 MiB is 3.125%; fine, but 1,000 × 8 KiB is ~7.8 MiB, so the two stated bounds are not simultaneously tight. State which is authoritative.

**Confirmations/refutations.** Round-7's D1 (resumption promise) is resolved — the current notice text makes no completion-time claim. Its P1 is resolved — RFC 8785 is now cited with divergences named. I agree the contract-9 LLM consult is doctrine-driven ceremony (P7 compliance), correctly denied authority — a non-LLM pipeline would suffice, but as specified it is harmless. The hold policy makes the audit subsystem gate all messaging; that blast radius is operator-approved and mitigated, so I flag it as accepted risk, not a defect.
